page.layout: One printed page, one column of verse running down the centre, with closing lines and signature below; faint show-through from the reverse side in the margins and over the text, not transcribed.

main_text.p: Immortalia ne speremus ager monet almus,.
main_text.l: Et Celer hora diei.
Nunc calathos onerant curvati pondere rami,
Fructibus æthereis:
Pendulus agricolæ ridet de palmite botrus:
Mox pede musta fluunt.
Gramina post fugiunt, spoliat virgulta November,
Bruma spuitque nives.
Luna tamen renovat cursus revolubilis anni;
Ast ubi nos cadimus
Et semel heu! gelidô clauduntur lumina lethô,
Pulvis & umbra sumus.
Quæritur hinc semper, quæ sint solamina nobis.
main_text.head: TU FRIDERICE decus
main_text.l: Musarum monstras, possit quis reddere faustos
Scilicet Omnipotens.
Secula nam vivet, qui mitia NUMINA sentit,
Nec moriturus erit.
O studii fœlix, ô fortunate laborum.
Jam BENEDICTE tuas,
Non moritura, fores, dudum jam gloria pulsat,
Alta volante comâ.
Illa manu palmamque ferens laurumque perennem.
Spretaque sic sequitur
Te tua laus, meritasque dabit post funera pompas.
Sic DOMINO valeas.

p.i: Cognato dilectissimo in solidi amoris signum posuit.

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly across the text and margins; not transcribed. The first line of verse is partly faded and the reading "Immortalia" is uncertain. The side note mark after "almus" is a doubtful reading and may be a printer's mark, not a true marginal note. The "Scilicet" line and the closing "FINIS" are set in larger or italic type and were read with some uncertainty.
